rules: Decompose before filing (itd-84, adopted 2026-08-15 at the MVP rung): before filing an intent, run the hand-run four-piece table documented in the /abcd:intent surface page — each part routed to its record home (capability -> intent; trust rule -> ADR + brief invariant; stance -> principle; plumbing -> brief), verdict FILE-AS-IS / SPLIT / HOLD, and a human confirms the routing.

Cross-record links are typed — supersedes / reverses / duplicates / refines — never a vague 'related'. A reversal flag is advisory-only: flagged for the human to confirm, never auto-classified, never auto-filed.

Not yet automated (loud-staging): the deterministic pre-pass and the capture-time validator are future rungs; until they ship the documented protocol is the gate. Grade every hand-run into the dated decomposition-calibration research note — the corpus that gates the automated rung.

Read the where-to-look playbook before hunting: .abcd/development/research/notes/2026-07-17-bug-hunting-principles.md — the spine, the value-ordered checklist (smell · failing question · CWE anchor), and the known gaps.

Spine: most defects are a wrong implicit assumption at a trust boundary that fails SILENTLY (ASCII-only, SHA-1-only, case-sensitive, one control range, first-occurrence-wins, clean env, parseable config). A fix is not done until every sibling site is swept — grep the pattern, not the instance.

Highest-leverage move: for each hardened primitive (gitutil.IsolatedEnv, fsutil.ReadGuarded, fsutil.WriteFileAtomic, refIsSafe, the (?i) identity matchers, lifeboat sanitize), grep for the unhardened sibling (raw os.Environ/os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile, a positional git arg, a case-sensitive matcher, a raw terminal print) and prove each is hardened or explicitly out of scope under the trusted-worktree model.
Markdown is the single source of truth; HTML is a generated, disposable artefact.
Docs are present tense only — what IS, never what was superseded or planned.
One Diataxis type per page (tutorial / how-to / reference / explanation).
User-facing prose in British English; code-side identifiers, comments, strings in US English.

Writing style: Follow the canonical guide at docs/reference/writing-style.md — em dashes allowed in prose but never in list items (use a colon), a capital letter after a colon, lower case after a semicolon. The guide labels each rule machine-enforced or review (the list-item em-dash rule is enforced as a docs-lint banned token; adr-54 rules the colon and semicolon casing checks review by nature); point at the guide rather than copying it.

Before presenting a drafted docs artefact (a page under docs/, README.md, or an edit to either), run `abcd lint docs` and clear its blockers first: the gate that will refuse the commit gives its feedback at draft time, not review time. Conversational replies are not artefacts and are never linted.
Intents are press-release-first; acceptance criteria are BDD (Given/When/Then).

Personas come from .abcd/development/personas.json: pick by role, never by name, and refer to every persona as they/them. The persona_registry record-lint rule enforces the registry (itd-79). (The bundled default names Alice/Bob/Carol for a registry-less adopter; this repo ships the registry, so the roster is the full fourteen.)
Lifecycle is drafts/ -> planned/ -> shipped/; a planned intent's adoption is the product thinker's decision.

The change that lands a planned intent's work closes its spec in the same change (go run ./cmd/abcd spec close <spc-N>), which ships the intent; nothing runs it for you, and a planned intent whose code is on main is invisible to the release cut.
A question to the human is asked ONE AT A TIME through the harness's interactive question tool, never as a numbered list inside prose; the next question waits for the answer to the last.
Each question is plain language a product thinker can answer without reading the record: one sentence of context, one concrete example of what each answer would mean in practice, then the options.

A question is put to the human only where two or more answers are each defensible on the record: widen-options-never-recommend governs conjectural questions, and where the record settles the answer, stating it is reporting, not recommending. The options are exactly those defensible answers plus the null answer, never alternatives manufactured to make up a set. A decision with one defensible answer is not asked at all; it is recorded as a decision line naming the answer and why no question was put.

What the human is asked to accept, edit or strike is quoted IN the question itself (the press release, the criterion, the text of each option), never referred to: 'are these criteria yours?' cannot be answered by someone who cannot see them, and prose written between tool calls is invisible while the question shows. Material too long for one question is put one part per question, a criterion at a time.

Options widen and never recommend (widen-options-never-recommend): no starred default, no '(recommended)' label, no ordering by the tool's preference, and the null answer ('none of these' / 'decide later') is always available. Where a recommendation is genuinely asked for, give it in prose apart from the question, and say when none is given.
Deferral is a real answer and is recorded as one; silence is never consent, and a step whose answer is missing is asked again rather than assumed.

Address the reader in their register: a product thinker gets outcomes and choices in product terms, no record ids, no code, no internals; a technical facilitator gets the mechanism, the ids and the trade-offs. When it is not known which hat the human wears, the first question asks that, and the itd-200 mode is the record of the answer.

Each register has a KNOWLEDGE FLOOR, and an explanation is measured against it, not only against its tone. The product thinker knows the product, its users, what done looks like and the ordinary vocabulary of using software (a file, a folder, a name, a version, an account, a link, a permission someone grants); they are not assumed to know version control (a checkout, a branch, a merge, a commit, a worktree), a shell, file ownership and permission bits, CI or a merge queue, a hook, an environment variable, a checksum, a symbolic link, or the record ids. The technical facilitator knows all of that as well, record ids and their lifecycles included, so explaining it to them is padding and leaving the ids out withholds the handle they act on.

An explanation for the product thinker names no tool and no mechanism below their floor. A concept that genuinely cannot be avoided is introduced in one sentence in product terms before it is used, without naming the tool that implements it (a repository is a project's folder of work, a lock is one person holding the pen, a checksum is a fingerprint saying two copies are identical). A question that fails this is rewritten, not annotated: a gloss after the jargon has already lost the reader.

Before stopping for a verdict, record whose answer is owed with the mode verb (`go run ./cmd/abcd mode facilitator` or `... mode product-thinker` in this checkout; the plugin-root binary's `mode` elsewhere), and set it back with `mode managed` once the answer is in. The set form prints one line naming the addressee where the host has no status surface; relay it verbatim, because that line is the whole of the fallback (itd-200).

The example that makes a question answerable goes IN the question text, and each option's preview carries what choosing that option means, with its own concrete example: prose written before the tool call is invisible while the question shows, so an example placed there is one the human never sees while choosing.

Classify each question's addressee FIRST (the product thinker or the technical facilitator); when it differs from the current mode label, set the label with the mode verb; then ask. The status-line label always names the person the question on screen is for, so a mixed interview re-sets it per question, never once at the start.

In a source checkout of abcd itself, every abcd invocation is `go run ./cmd/abcd <verb>` from the repo root — never the plugin-root binary and never an `abcd` on PATH. Both are the last PUBLISHED version, stale by construction here and further behind with every commit, and the failure is often silent rather than a refusal: an empty `changelog --json` cut, a record written through a schema the gates no longer accept. The documented resolution ladder reaches the plugin-root binary first and it answers, so the `go run` fallback is never reached by following it; go straight to `go run ./cmd/abcd` (AGENTS.md, Build, test, and checks).

Phases and milestones are retired (adr-2609212115255771): sequencing is dependencies (blocked_by, builds_on) plus the lifecycle shelves, rendered as the Now / Next / Later status block; the checkpoint is the derived release plus each intent's acceptance criteria; an intent that must land by a cut carries target_release, which the cut reports and moves forward.
No time estimates and no roadmap document: the press-release intent format carries priority; the word roadmap is retired and the phase documents under roadmap/ are history.
